task.name: A gate verdict that does not reproduce aborts a sprint before any work begins, and the same gate passes on the next run with nothing changed
task.story_text:
## Observed

The gate returns FAIL, and returns PASS on the next invocation against the same commit, the same
machine and an unchanged working tree. When that first verdict is the one guarding a sprint launch,
the sprint aborts before any dev work starts and the money spent reaching that point is lost.

Three occurrences in two days, all on the same release branch:

- **2026-08-12, release-candidate cut.** The gate failed on one test out of 8,381, in sandbox
  group-kill teardown. That test then passed three times standalone, its whole file passed fourteen
  of fourteen under parallel execution three times, and the full gate passed on re-run twenty minutes
  later with nothing changed. The cut had to be repeated.
- **2026-08-13, sprint baseline.** The sprint's baseline gate failed on two tests out of 8,399, in
  process-tree traversal. The sprint terminated abnormally with `Broken baseline: configured gate
  failed on sprint merge base ... before any dev work started`. Cost at abort was $19.29. One of the
  three queued stories never started and the overnight window was lost. The same gate, run against
  the same commit immediately afterwards, passed with 8,399 passed and 0 failed.
- **Earlier, during a code review.** A reviewer running the full suite reported seventeen failures,
  all sandbox permission errors in multiprocessing semaphore creation and temporary file naming, and
  judged them unrelated to the change under review.

Every failing test in all three has involved process groups, process trees, forking or sandbox
teardown. None has ever reproduced on a targeted re-run. The suite emits, on each of these runs,
`DeprecationWarning: This process is multi-threaded, use of fork() may lead to deadlocks in the
child`.

The failures are also not attributable to what landed. In the sprint-baseline case the two commits
on the branch touched only the dev-phase retry path and two unrelated test modules, neither of which
is exercised by the tests that failed.

## Expected

A check whose verdict decides whether work may begin returns the same verdict for the same inputs. A
result that cannot be reproduced against the same commit is not evidence about that commit, and is
not used to refuse work or to end a run that has already been paid for.

Where a check cannot be made deterministic, a failure it produces is distinguishable from one that
reflects the state being checked, so an operator is not required to re-run it by hand to learn which
kind they are looking at. Repeating an expensive operation to find out whether its refusal was real
is the cost this creates, and it falls on whoever happened to be running when it fired.

Where work is abandoned on the strength of such a verdict, what was spent reaching that point is
reported, since an abort before work begins still consumes budget and an operator deciding whether to
retry needs to know what the attempt cost.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `9b5c62318cee67dd47fd4bf0f9c951d64c14af1b` captured at `2026-08-13T12:24:16.940921+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:9895897ced3118f4aac70e7a4268a129b28eda7acb7a63ce39b33b0121779777`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py` — `sha256:37fb741f90df8f97e9fe71b7ad9fc1ed6be047fe64fe035c2be780aa907ac91f`
- `tests/test_sprint_baseline_gate.py` — `sha256:208111dcd3dc263469aaf602e355c780bb2bc5d0ee06697f223886763ea2371a`
- `tests/test_process_group.py` — `sha256:501312bdafecdcb847542588df115fb68bde6d36d73c020ade5d4199192dbdf5`
- `src/theforge/process_group.py` — `sha256:a20e20f29029fd426e9cd41e67fb9bd410b281d06cf705fcf2f81498c41e8aac`
- `src/theforge/process_tree.py` — `sha256:ba6af4a126c1fd153c071d675cb19c8466666c53f24f62f70c17e04cf3b7997e`

### Observed symptom

The sprint baseline gate (the check run against the merge base before any dev
iteration starts) executes the configured gate command exactly once. A single
non-zero exit is treated as definitive proof the merge base is broken: the
sprint is aborted with a "Broken baseline" RuntimeError and no story ever
starts. When the failing tests are process-group/sandbox-teardown flakes, the
identical gate command passes minutes later against the identical commit with
nothing changed — so the abort was not evidence about the commit, it was
evidence about one noisy invocation. Separately, when this abort fires after
entry-level intake remediation has already spent money, the sprint audit
records the run's cost as a hardcoded 0.0, so the spend that produced the
abort is invisible to the operator.

### Reproduction / evidence

src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1488 — `_run_baseline_gate` calls
`run_gate_full(...)` exactly once against a fresh worktree of the merge base;
there is no retry, no re-run-to-confirm, and no flake/infra-vs-regression
classification anywhere in this function. Any FAIL decision goes straight to
the `message = "Broken baseline: configured gate failed on sprint merge base
..."` branch at line 1523.

src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:4753-4779 — in `run_sprint`, when
`baseline_gate["passed"]` is falsy, `_write_sprint_audit` is called with
`total_cost_usd=0.0` (line 4762) hardcoded, and then `RuntimeError` is raised
(line 4779). The entry-intake remediation cost-folding logic that would
attribute already-spent money to the sprint total
(`_entry_intake_cost = sum(...)` / `_sprint_state.cost.add(_entry_intake_cost)`,
lines 4799-4805) sits *after* this abort point in the function body and is
never reached when the baseline gate fails — so any spend incurred before the
baseline gate ran (e.g. the CLI's pre-`run_sprint` entry-level intake
remediation pass, the reported $19.29 in the 2026-08-13 occurrence) is not in
the audit's cost field.

Corroborating: the 2026-08-12 RC cut and 2026-08-13 sprint-baseline failures
both cite process-group/process-tree/sandbox-teardown tests that never
reproduced on a targeted re-run, and both suite runs emitted the
multi-threaded-fork() DeprecationWarning — consistent with sandbox/process
teardown flakiness rather than a code regression, but `_run_baseline_gate` has
no mechanism to tell the two apart before treating FAIL as final.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** The baseline gate runs the configured command once and treats any non-zero exit as a definitive, reproducible verdict, with no re-run or confirmation step before aborting the sprint.
  - Evidence: run_gate_full is called exactly once in _run_baseline_gate (runner.py:1488); the FAIL branch (line 1523) goes straight to raising RuntimeError with no retry logic anywhere in the function or its caller.
- **[confirmed]** The specific tests failing are genuinely flaky under this project's sandbox/process-group teardown, which the gate has no way to distinguish from a real regression.
  - Evidence: All three occurrences involve process-group/process-tree/sandbox-teardown tests, none reproduced on targeted or standalone re-run, and the suite emits the multi-threaded fork() DeprecationWarning on these runs — a known class of nondeterministic failure, not something introduced by the commits under test (the sprint-baseline occurrence's only two commits touched dev-phase retry logic and unrelated test modules).
- **[ruled out]** The commits on the branch caused the failures (a real regression that happened to also stop reproducing).
  - Evidence: Issue states the two commits on the branch touched only the dev-phase retry path and two unrelated test modules, neither exercised by the failing tests; the same gate against the same commit passed cleanly (8,399/8,399) minutes later with the tree unchanged.
- **[ruled out]** Spend already incurred before the baseline gate runs (e.g. entry-level intake remediation) is folded into the aborted sprint's audit, so the reported cost figure comes from existing accounting.
  - Evidence: The broken-baseline audit write at runner.py:4762 hardcodes total_cost_usd=0.0; the only code that folds entry-intake remediation cost into the sprint total (runner.py:4799-4805) executes strictly after the baseline-gate abort check and is unreachable when the gate fails.

### Confirmed cause

`_run_baseline_gate` (src/theforge/sprint/runner.py) invokes the configured
gate command a single time against a temporary worktree of the merge base and
treats that one FAIL as conclusive: `run_sprint` immediately writes a
"broken_baseline" sprint audit and raises, ending the sprint before any story
starts. There is no re-run to confirm the failure is reproducible and no
mechanism to distinguish a nondeterministic sandbox/process-teardown failure
from a real defect in the merge base. Compounding this, the audit written at
that abort point hardcodes `total_cost_usd=0.0` (runner.py:4762) rather than
including money already spent before the baseline gate ran (e.g. entry-level
intake remediation, whose cost-folding logic at runner.py:4799-4805 sits after
the abort and never executes on this path) — so an operator cannot see what
the aborted attempt cost.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1269-1600 (`_run_baseline_gate`, single
run_gate_full call at line 1488, FAIL handling from line 1523);
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:4736-4779 (`run_sprint`'s baseline-gate abort
branch, hardcoded total_cost_usd=0.0 at line 4762, RuntimeError raise at line
4779, entry-intake cost folding at lines 4799-4805 unreachable on this path).

### Fix-success criterion

(1) A baseline-gate FAIL that does not reproduce on an immediate re-run
against the identical worktree/commit does not, by itself, abort the sprint
or produce a "Broken baseline" verdict — the gate result is either confirmed
by a second run before being treated as final, or the ambiguous outcome is
surfaced distinguishably from a reproducible failure so an operator does not
have to re-run the suite by hand to find out which it was. (2) When a sprint
does abort on a broken-baseline verdict, the sprint audit's cost field
reflects money actually spent reaching that point (including any pre-gate
entry-intake remediation spend) rather than an unconditional 0.0.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- The underlying process-group/sandbox-teardown test flakiness (multi-threaded fork() DeprecationWarning, semaphore/tempfile races under parallel test execution) is not itself diagnosed here and likely needs its own fix in the test suite's sandbox/process-teardown handling.
- Per-story dev-iteration gates (validate_phase.py) have retry/escalate routing across dev attempts, but that retries by having the dev change code, not by re-running an identical gate to confirm a flake — the same non-reproducible-failure risk may apply there too, out of this issue's scope.

### Notes

I did not trace the RC-cut path (scripts/cut-rc.sh) or the code-review full-suite
run in detail — both are separate invocations of the same underlying flaky
test class and corroborate the pattern, but the concrete, fixable mechanism
with clear cost consequences is the sprint-launch baseline gate in
runner.py, which is also what the issue's "Expected" section (spend
reporting on abort) points at most directly. The root cause of *why* the
process-group/sandbox-teardown tests themselves are flaky (the
multi-threaded fork() warning, semaphore/tempfile races) is not diagnosed
here — that is a test-suite reliability issue, not this issue's stated
symptom (gate verdicts not being treated as reproducible, and lost spend not
being reported). It belongs in related_findings / a separate issue.

handoff.summary: The sprint baseline gate now confirms a failure before treating it as the merge base's verdict: on a FAIL, run_gate_full is invoked a second time against the identical temporary worktree and commit, before the evidence-capture/worktree-preservation block. Only a reproduced failure halts the sprint; a non-reproduced one returns passed=True with status pass_unreproduced_failure, falls through the ordinary cleanup path (no preserved worktree), writes the first run's full output under a distinct -unreproduced-failure.txt filename, and carries confirmation_attempted / failure_reproduced / initial_result / confirmation_result into the sprint audit's baseline_check. run_sprint publishes a phase detail when the confirmation run starts so forge status does not read as stuck, and emits a structured baseline_gate_failure_not_reproduced log line when it proceeds past a non-reproduced failure. Separately, the entry-intake remediation cost fold was extracted to _fold_entry_intake_cost and moved ahead of the broken-baseline abort branch, whose SprintResult now reports _sprint_state.cost.spent instead of a hardcoded 0.0. docs/flake-register.md records that a non-reproduced baseline failure is a flake candidate, not a pass.

plan_review.findings:
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (a rare intermittently-real regression is admitted as a flake) is carried, not retired: the plan's mitigation is metadata only, and no step makes the non-reproduced outcome visible in the operator-facing sprint log/CLI beyond the audit dict. This does not threaten either acceptance criterion — AC1 explicitly permits proceeding when the failure does not reproduce — so it is recorded rather than blocking.
  Suggestion: Have Step 1 also emit a structured log line (via _sprint_logger.emit / _log, as the baseline_gate_skipped path at runner.py:4730 does) when the sprint proceeds past a non-reproduced baseline failure, so the ambiguity is visible without reading the audit JSON.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (double-counting entry-intake spend) is only partially retired: Step 4 tests the abort path's cost, but no step tests that the normal (baseline-passes) path still folds entry-intake cost exactly once after the block moves.
  Suggestion: Move the block rather than duplicating it, and add an assertion in the passing-baseline test that _sprint_state.cost reflects the entry-intake spend exactly once.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 does not say what happens to worktree preservation and evidence capture on the non-reproduced path. The FAIL branch deliberately preserves the temporary worktree and writes .forge/logs evidence (#2160, runner.py:~1545-1600); if the confirmation run passes, the function must fall through to the normal cleanup path or every flaky first run leaks a preserved worktree.
  Suggestion: Perform the confirmation run before the evidence-capture/worktree-preservation block, and on a passing confirmation return through the existing pass path so normal cleanup runs — optionally still writing the first run's output as evidence under a distinct filename.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] A confirmation run doubles baseline-gate wall time whenever the first run fails (the cited suites are 8,000+ tests, ~20 minutes), and the plan does not mention a timeout or budget interaction for the second invocation.
  Suggestion: Reuse the existing gate timeout resolution for the confirmation run and note the re-run in the phase detail published via _publish_sprint_phase so forge status does not look stuck.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Confirm baseline-gate failures before treating them as broken-baseline verdicts: run the configured gate once, immediately re-run the identical gate only after a failure, and allow the sprint to continue when the failure does not reproduce while recording that ambiguity in the returned gate metadata. Move existing pre-gate intake cost folding ahead of the baseline abort branch so broken-baseline audits report actual spend.

steps.details: In _run_baseline_gate, keep the current single successful-run path unchanged. When the first run_gate_full result fails, immediately invoke run_gate_full a second time against the same temporary baseline worktree and merge-base commit. Return passed=false only when the second run also fails, and include metadata distinguishing confirmed failures from non-reproduced first failures, such as confirmation_attempted, initial_result, confirmation_result, and failure_reproduced. When the second run passes, return passed=true with non-reproduced failure metadata so run_sprint does not raise Broken baseline for that invocation.

steps.description: Surface confirmed versus non-reproduced baseline outcomes in sprint audit data
steps.details: Preserve the existing broken_baseline abort behavior for confirmed failures, but ensure the baseline_gate dict written to audit includes the confirmation metadata from _run_baseline_gate. Add or update tests so a first failed gate followed by a passing confirmation does not abort and records the non-reproduced outcome, while two failed gate runs still abort as broken_baseline.

steps.description: Report actual spend on broken-baseline aborts
steps.details: Move the existing entry-intake remediation cost folding that reads _ctx.entry_intake_outcomes and adds through SprintExecutionState.cost before the baseline_gate passed check, making it idempotent for the normal path. Replace the broken-baseline audit's hardcoded total_cost_usd=0.0 with the current value from SprintExecutionState.cost when constructing SprintResult.

Extend baseline-gate abort coverage so a confirmed baseline failure after pre-gate entry-intake remediation writes a sprint audit whose total_cost_usd reflects the already-recorded remediation spend instead of zero.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A baseline-gate FAIL that does not reproduce on an immediate re-run against the identical worktree/commit does not, by itself, abort the sprint or produce a Broken baseline verdict; the gate result is either confirmed by a second run before being treated as final, or the ambiguous outcome is surfaced distinguishably.

When a sprint does abort on a broken-baseline verdict, the sprint audit's cost field reflects money actually spent reaching that point, including any pre-gate entry-intake remediation spend, rather than an unconditional 0.0.

risks.description: Treating one failure followed by one pass as allowed work may hide a rare real regression that is itself intermittent.
risks.mitigation: Record explicit non-reproduced baseline metadata in the audit so operators can see that the launch proceeded after a failed first invocation and investigate recurring flakes separately.

risks.description: Moving entry-intake cost folding earlier could double-count if the normal path still executes the old block.
risks.mitigation: Move the existing block rather than copying it, or guard the ledger addition so the same entry-intake outcomes are folded exactly once through SprintExecutionState.cost.

risks.description: The exact baseline_gate dict shape may have downstream consumers not visible in the focused tests.
risks.mitigation: Only add optional metadata fields and preserve existing keys and passed semantics so current consumers remain compatible.
